commonly known as '''Bayer Leverkusen''' or simply '''Leverkusen''', is a German professional [[association football|football]] club based in [[Leverkusen]], [[North Rhine-Westphalia]].{{cite web |title=Sports – moving moments |url=http://www.nrwinvest.com/NRW_at_a_glance/Facts_Figures/Sports/index.php |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141015161207/http://www.nrwinvest.com/NRW_at_a_glance/Facts_Figures/Sports/index.php |archive-date=15 October 2014 |access-date=9 October 2014 |work=NRW Invest}} It competes in the [[Bundesliga]], the top tier of [[German football league system|German football]], and plays its home matches at the [[BayArena]].{{cite web |url=http://www.bundesliga.com/en/liga/clubs/bayer-leverkusen/daten.php |title=Bayer 04 Leverkusen – Club Data |website=bundesliga.com |publisher=Deutsche Fußball Liga |access-date=9 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141013103620/http://www.bundesliga.com/en/liga/clubs/bayer-leverkusen/daten.php |archive-date=13 October 2014 |url-status=dead }} Founded in 1904 by employees of the paint factory, today better known as a pharmaceutical company [[Bayer]] (whose headquarters are in Leverkusen and from which the club draws its name), the club was formerly a department of TSV Bayer 04 Leverkusen [[sports club]] whose members participate in athletics, gymnastics, [[Bayer Giants Leverkusen|basketball]], field and handball. In 1999, the football department was separated from the sports club. Bayer Leverkusen's main colours are red and black, which feature across their playing kits and badge, and their main rival is [[1. FC Köln]],{{cite web |url=http://www.bayer04.de/B04-ENG/en/_md_aktuell-dt.aspx?aktuell=aktuell-5267 |title=FC Köln derby a Saturday fixture |work=Bayer Leverkusen |date=25 September 2014 |access-date=9 October 2014 |archive-date=28 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220228144836/https://www.bayer04.de/B04-ENG/en/_md_aktuell-dt.aspx?aktuell=aktuell-5267 |url-status=live }} while the fans have had a deep friendship with the supporters of [[Kickers Offenbach]] for almost 50 years.{{Cite web |title=#BayerundderOFC – Friendly for a good cause |url=https://www.bayer04.de/en-us/news/bayer04/bayerundderofc-friendly-for-a-good-cause |access-date=11 August 2025 |website=Bayer 04 Leverkusen Fussball GmbH |language=en}} Bayer Leverkusen were promoted to the Bundesliga in [[1978–79 2. Bundesliga|1979]] and won their maiden top-flight honor, the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]], in [[1987–88 UEFA Cup|1988]]. The club won its first domestic honour, the [[DFB Pokal]], in [[1992–93 DFB-Pokal|1993]]. The club finished runners-up across three competitions in 2002, including the [[2001–02 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]]. After over 30 years without silverware, the club won their [[2023–24 Bundesliga|first Bundesliga title]] and their second [[2023–24 DFB-Pokal|DFB Pokal]] in 2024,{{Cite web |url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/bayer-leverkusen-are-2023-24-bundesliga-champions-26930 |title=Bayer Leverkusen are 2023/24 Bundesliga champions! |website=bundesliga.com |publisher=Deutsche Fußball Liga |date=14 April 2024 |access-date=14 April 2024 |url-status=live |archive-date=14 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240414175118/https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/bayer-leverkusen-are-2023-24-bundesliga-champions-26930}}{{cite web |url=http://www.bayer04.de/b04-eng/en/_site_index.aspx |title=Bayer 04 Honours |work=Bayer Leverkusen |access-date=9 October 2014 |archive-date=27 September 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130927150152/http://www.bayer04.de/b04-eng/en/_site_index.aspx |url-status=live }} becoming the first German team to win the league or [[Double (association football)|domestic double]] [[List of unbeaten football club seasons#Europe|unbeaten]], while setting the [[European association football club records and statistics#Longest unbeaten run across all competitions|European record for consecutive unbeaten competitive games]] (51). ==History== ===Origins and early years=== On 27 November 1903, Wilhelm Hauschild wrote a letter – signed by 180 of his fellow workers – to his employer, the [[Bayer|Friedrich Bayer and Co.]], seeking the company's support in starting a sports club.{{cite web |url=http://www.bayer04.de/B04-ENG/en/1282.aspx?guid=1282-AAE73455-851F-436A-9709-1746E89C1C26 |title=The Early Years – It all Started with a Letter |publisher=Bayer 04 Leverkusen |access-date=9 October 2014 |archive-date=14 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141014162018/http://www.bayer04.de/B04-ENG/en/1282.aspx?guid=1282-AAE73455-851F-436A-9709-1746E89C1C26 |url-status=live }} The company agreed to support the initiative, and on 1 July 1904 ''Turn- und Spielverein Bayer 04 Leverkusen'' was founded as a [[works team]]. On 31 May 1907, a separate football department was formed within the club. In the culture of sports in Germany at the time, there was significant animosity between gymnasts and other types of athletes. Eventually this contributed to a split within the club: on 8 June 1928, the footballers formed a separate association – ''Sportvereinigung Bayer 04 Leverkusen'' – that also included the [[handball]] and [[fistball]] players, athletics, and [[boxing]], while the gymnasts carried on as ''TuS Bayer 04 Leverkusen''.{{Cite web |title=1920s |url=https://www.bayer04.de/en-us/page/history/founding-years-to-the-new-millennium/1920s |access-date=10 August 2025 |website=Bayer 04 Leverkusen Fussball GmbH |language=en}} ''SV Bayer 04 Leverkusen'' took with them the club's traditional colours of red and black, with the gymnasts adopting blue and yellow after a while. Until 1930, Wiesdorf was the hometown of Bayer 04, and Leverkusen was merely the district where the factories and workers' housing were located. In 1930, Wiesdorf and the neighboring municipalities merged to form a new town. They named it Leverkusen because of the factory's importance, among other things, for the community's growth. Thus, the club now bore the name of its city.{{Cite web |title=1930s |url=https://www.bayer04.de/en-us/page/history/founding-years-to-the-new-millennium/1930s |access-date=11 August 2025 |website=Bayer 04 Leverkusen Fussball GmbH |language=en}} [[File:Bayer Leverkusen Performance Chart.png|upright=2.0|thumb|200px|Historical chart of Bayer Leverkusen league performance after WWII]] Through this period, and into the 1930s, SV Bayer 04 Leverkusen played third and fourth division football. In 1936, they earned promotion to the second highest class of play of the period.{{cite web |url=http://www.bayer04.de/B04-ENG/en/1283.aspx?guid=1283-687E6C91-5980-405A-B82C-E1DFBCE4C5F7 |title=The Thirties – The Bayer Emblem on the Shirt |work=Bayer Leverkusen |access-date=9 October 2014 |archive-date=14 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141014162232/http://www.bayer04.de/B04-ENG/en/1283.aspx?guid=1283-687E6C91-5980-405A-B82C-E1DFBCE4C5F7 |url-status=live }} That was also the year that the club wore the "'''''Bayer'''''" cross, still visible on their kits, for the first time. They made their first appearance in upper league play in 1951, in the [[Oberliga West (1947–63)|Oberliga West]] and played there until 1956, after which they were relegated. [[File:StadionAmStadtpark.jpg|thumb|300px|A freekick in the old stadium ''Stadtpark'' against SV Sodingen in 1955]] ''SV Bayer 04 Leverkusen'' would not return to the upper leagues until 1962, just one season before the formation of Germany's new professional league, the [[Bundesliga]]. The next year saw the club in the [[Regionalliga West (1963–74)|Regionalliga West]], tier II. ===2. Bundesliga to Bundesliga, UEFA Cup, and DFB-Pokal=== After not having been among the top teams in the second-tier Regionalliga SV Bayer 04 Leverkusen made something of a breakthrough in 1968 by sensationally winning the division title (with only 15 men in the squad), but was unable to advance to the playoff round to the first division. The club was relegated again in 1973, but made a quick return to what was now called the [[2. Bundesliga]] after just one season spent in the third division. Four years later, the club secured a place in the Bundesliga to start to play there in the [[1979–80 Bundesliga|1979–80 season.]] By the mid-1980s, SV Bayer 04 Leverkusen had become established in the upper half of the league table and was well-established there by the end of the decade. It was during this time, in 1984, that the two halves of the club that had parted ways over a half century earlier were re-united as '''TSV Bayer 04 Leverkusen e.V.''' The new club took red and white as its colours. Although the football department officially retained the colors black and red, the "Werkself" played in red and white for the next ten years. In addition to becoming an established Bundesliga side, the club earned its first honours with a win in the [[1987–88 UEFA Cup|1988 UEFA Cup]]. Down 0–3 to [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] after the first leg of the final, Bayer Leverkusen drew even in the return match and then won the title on penalty kicks, 3–2.{{cite web |url=http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/season=1987/overview/index.html |title=1987/88: Resurgent Leverkusen hold their nerve |publisher=UEFA |date=1 June 1988 |access-date=9 October 2014 |archive-date=7 April 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140407124031/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/season=1987/overview/index.html |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/nationalassociations/teams/50109--leverkusen/ |title=Leverkusen |publisher=UEFA |access-date=9 October 2014 |archive-date=19 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141019040241/http://www.uefa.com/teamsandplayers/teams/club=50109/profile/index.html |url-status=live }} That same year, long-time Bayer Leverkusen executive Reiner Calmund became the general manager of the club. The decade and a half following this saw club's greatest successes. After the [[German reunification]] in 1990, Reiner Calmund was quick to sign prominent [[East Germany|East German]] players [[Ulf Kirsten]] and [[Andreas Thom]].{{Cite web |title=1990–1991 |url=https://www.bayer04.de/en-us/page/history/seasons/1990-1991 |access-date=11 August 2025 |website=Bayer 04 Leverkusen Fussball GmbH |language=en}} After they were able to sign [[Matthias Sammer]], who later became a world footballer, Chancellor [[Helmut Kohl]] vetoed the deal.{{Cite web |title=Ausverkauf des DDR-Fußballs?: Wie Reiner Calmund Andreas Thom in den Westen lockte |url=https://www.mz.de/sport/fussball/ausverkauf-des-ddr-fussballs-wie-reiner-calmund-andreas-thom-in-den-westen-lockte-3137789 |access-date=11 August 2025 |website=Mitteldeutsche Zeitung |language=de}} Calmund also established contacts in [[Football in Brazil|Brazilian football]] through [[Sports agent#Association football|player agent]] Juan Figer. Between 1987 and 1993, the club signed Brazilian internationals [[Jorginho (footballer, born 1964)|Jorginho]] and [[Paulo Sérgio (footballer, born June 1969)|Paulo Sérgio]]. During this period, Leverkusen also acquired prominent German players, including [[Bernd Schuster]] and [[Rudi Völler]], which helped increase the team's public profile and competitive performances.{{Cite web |title=Völler: ‘With the cross on the chest – in good and bad times!’ {{!}} Bayer04.de |url=https://www.bayer04.de/en-us/news/bayer04/voeller-with-the-cross-on-the-chest-in-good-and-bad-times |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=Bayer 04 Leverkusen Fussball GmbH |language=en}}{{Cite web |first= |date=2024-04-14 |title=No more Neverkusen as Bayer Leverkusen win Bundesliga title at last |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/no-more-neverkusen-bayer-leverkusen-181325604.html |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US}} The club won its next major honour in 1993 with a 1–0 win in the [[DFB-Pokal]] final against [[Hertha BSC]] second team (amateur squad) on 12 June 1993.{{cite web |url=http://www.fussballdaten.de/dfb/1993/ |title=DFB Cup 1992/1993 |work=Fussball Daten |access-date=9 October 2014 |archive-date=26 October 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161026013603/http://www.fussballdaten.de/dfb/1993/ |url-status=live }} In the following season, in a game in which Schuster scored a 45 metre "German Goal of the Year" (a goal which was later also named "Goal of the Decade"). {{Commons|Bayer 04 Leverkusen kits}} After the club had almost been relegated in 1996 they regularly found themselves among the top three of the league under new coach [[Christoph Daum]]. In the next years they sign players such as [[Lúcio]], [[Emerson (footballer, born 1976)|Emerson]], [[Zé Roberto]] and [[Michael Ballack]]. Daum was later fired for a [[cocaine]] scandal that also cost him his ascent to the role of the [[Germany national football team|Germany national team]] coach.{{vague|date=January 2024|reason=was he Germany national team coach? or was he about to be appointed Germany national team coach? or is all this speculative?}}{{cite web |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/15/germany/2010/11/19/2220135/germany-unity-series-from-messiah-to-judas-christoph-daum |title=Germany Unity Series: From Messiah To Judas – Christoph Daum and the Cocaine Scandal |work=Goal (website) |date=19 November 2010 |access-date=9 October 2014 |archive-date=4 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141004102057/http://www.goal.com/en/news/15/germany/2010/11/19/2220135/germany-unity-series-from-messiah-to-judas-christoph-daum |url-status=live }}{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2009/may/20/seven-deadly-sins-football-gluttony-part-two |title=Gluttony – part two |work=The Guardian |date=20 May 2009 |access-date=9 October 2014 |archive-date=20 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141020062634/http://www.theguardian.com/football/2009/may/20/seven-deadly-sins-football-gluttony-part-two |url-status=live }} ==="Neverkusen"=== [[File:Ulf Kirsten.jpg|thumb|200px|[[Ulf Kirsten]], three-time Bundesliga top scorer]] Leverkusen earned a series of four second-place finishes from 1997 to 2002. Most notably, the team had the Bundesliga title within their grasp in 2000 and 2002.{{Cite web |last=O'Connor |first=Robert |date=30 September 2021 |title=The horror treble: remembering the worst collapse in European football |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/horror-treble-remembering-worst-collapse-european-football |access-date=24 February 2024 |website=fourfourtwo.com |language=en |archive-date=24 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240224172807/https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/horror-treble-remembering-worst-collapse-european-football |url-status=live }} In 2000, Leverkusen needed only a draw against [[SpVgg Unterhaching]] to win the title, but an own goal by Michael Ballack helped send the team to a heart-wrenching 2–0 defeat, while [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] won the title with a 3–1 victory over [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]]. Two years later, the club surrendered a five-point lead atop the league table by losing two of its last three matches, while [[Borussia Dortmund]] swept ahead{{tone inline|date=January 2024}} with three consecutive victories in its final matches. The 2002 season has been dubbed{{by whom|date=January 2024}} the "Treble Horror", as Leverkusen were also beaten 4–2 in the [[2002 DFB-Pokal final|DFB-Pokal final]] by [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]] and [[File:Bayarena Leverkusen 2020.jpg|thumb|250px|[[BayArena]], the stadium of Bayer Leverkusen]] The 50+1 rule in German football states that a club must hold at least 50 percent of the voting rights plus one vote in its spun-off corporation in order to maintain control. The goal is to limit the influence of external investors and protect the club's structure. However, there are two exceptions: Leverkusen and [[VfL Wolfsburg]]. Because these clubs were founded as works clubs and the corresponding companies supported the club financially, among other things, for many decades, the football department of Bayer 04 was spun off from the overall club in 1999 and has been a subsidiary of Bayer AG ever since. This allows to offset financial losses at the end of a fiscal year, but also requires profits to be transferred.{{Cite web |title=Explaining the Bundesliga's 50+1 rule |url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/50-1-fifty-plus-one-german-football-soccer-rule-explained-ownership-22832 |access-date=10 August 2025 |website=www.bundesliga.com |language=en}} However, a ruling by the Federal Cartel Office from 2025 identifies a need for improvements regarding the exemptions. Therefore, it can be assumed that the German Football League (DFL) will demand more say for the parent club TSV Bayer 04 Leverkusen e.V. in the future, or that members will have to be more closely
